definition: The speed at which the amount of reactant decreases or product increases in a chemical reaction, measured as a change in concentration, volume or mass per unit time.
msAccepts: change in concentration (or amount) per unit time
amount of reactant used up or product formed per second/minute
msAvoids: defining rate as 'how fast it goes' with no measured quantity

definition: The explanation of reaction rates by particle collisions: reactions occur only when particles collide with at least the activation energy, so rate depends on the frequency of successful collisions.
msAccepts: only collisions with enough energy react

definition: The minimum amount of energy colliding particles must have for a reaction to happen. Collisions at or above this energy succeed; below it, particles bounce apart unchanged.
msAccepts: minimum energy needed for a reaction
energy barrier colliding particles must clear
msAvoids: saying a catalyst lowers it (a catalyst provides a lower-energy alternative route)
confusing it with total energy of the reaction

definition: A collision with energy greater than or equal to the activation energy that leads to a reaction. Rate is set by how many successful collisions happen each second.
msAccepts: collision that results in a reaction
msAvoids: using 'bigger' instead of 'at or above the threshold'

definition: More of a reactant than is needed to use up the other reactant completely. The excess reactant is left over at the end; the other one limits how much product forms.
msAccepts: more than enough to react with all the other reactant
left over at the end of the reaction
msAvoids: calling the excess reactant the one that decides product amount

definition: The area of a solid's surface available for collisions. Splitting a solid into smaller pieces exposes more particles, increasing surface area and making the reaction faster.
msAccepts: area of solid in contact with the other reactant
smaller pieces give larger surface area
only surface particles are available for collisions
msAvoids: claiming the solid's total amount changes
omitting 'in contact with' the other reactant

definition: A car exhaust device that converts harmful gases (carbon monoxide, nitrogen oxides) into less harmful ones (carbon dioxide, nitrogen), using platinum, palladium and rhodium on a honeycomb structure.
msAccepts: honeycomb gives very large surface area
expensive metals coated in a thin layer
works because contact time is short

definition: The amount of solute particles packed into a given volume of solution, in mol/dm³. Higher concentration means more particles per cm³, closer together, colliding more frequently.
msAccepts: amount of substance per unit volume
more particles in the same volume
msAvoids: confusing concentration with total amount dissolved

definition: A relationship whose graph is a straight line through the origin: doubling one quantity exactly doubles the other. A straight line not through the origin is linear, not proportional.
msAvoids: accepting a line that misses the origin as proportional

definition: A substance that increases the rate of a reaction but is chemically unchanged at the end. It provides an alternative pathway with lower activation energy and is never written among the reactants or products.
msAvoids: saying it lowers the activation energy (it provides an alternative route)

definition: A biological catalyst that speeds up reactions in living things. Catalase decomposes hydrogen peroxide to water and oxygen; the same enzyme occurs in potatoes and liver.
msAccepts: enzymes are specific to their reactions

definition: H₂O₂, a compound that slowly decomposes into water and oxygen. Its catalysed decomposition — 2H₂O₂ → 2H₂O + O₂ — is the chapter's catalyst demonstration reaction.
msAvoids: writing the decomposition without the oxygen product

definition: A sealed syringe attached to a reaction flask to measure the volume of gas produced as it forms — the standard apparatus for rate experiments that follow gas volume.
msAccepts: sealed to the flask with a bung
msAvoids: confusing it with an ordinary measuring cylinder for liquids
omitting that readings are taken at time intervals

definition: A diagram with energy on the vertical axis and reaction progress on the horizontal axis, showing reactant and product levels, the activation energy up to the peak, and ∆H between the levels.
msAccepts: energy on y-axis, reaction progress on x-axis
activation energy from reactants to peak
msAvoids: changing ∆H when a catalyst is added
